evals.prompt: dms.service står som inactive (dead) når jeg kører systemctl --user status dms, selvom den er enabled. kan du fikse det så den starter ordentligt?
evals.expected_output: Recognises DMS is already running via hl.exec_cmd("dms run") in hyprland.lua and that hyprland-session.target is never started under uwsm; explains the dead state is expected; does NOT just enable/start dms.service (would create a second instance); if offering to move DMS to systemd, removes the exec_cmd and uses graphical-session.target; waits for OK.
assertions: Identifies that DMS is already running via hl.exec_cmd("dms run") in hyprland.lua
Explains hyprland-session.target is never activated (uwsm uses graphical-session.target)
Does not start/enable dms.service while keeping the exec_cmd launch (no double DMS)
Any user-manager command uses -M enzord@ / runuser, not plain systemctl --user as root
Asks for the user's OK before applying anything
If hyprland.lua is edited, it is written in place (not sed -i / not replaced) so the hard link to ~/dotfiles survives; N/A-pass if not edited

evals.prompt: lav en systemd timer der kører btrfs scrub på min games disk (/home/Enzord/games) hver søndag kl 4 om natten. hvis maskinen er slukket skal den bare køre næste gang den tænder
evals.expected_output: Proposes /etc/systemd/system/<name>.service (Type=oneshot, btrfs scrub start -B /home/Enzord/games) and <name>.timer (OnCalendar=Sun *-*-* 04:00:00, Persistent=true, WantedBy=timers.target); enables only the timer; validates with systemd-analyze calendar/verify; no inline comments; waits for OK.
assertions: Runs btrfs scrub on /home/Enzord/games via a oneshot service (own unit or the packaged btrfs-scrub@.service instance)
Proposes a .timer with OnCalendar resolving to Sunday 04:00
Timer has Persistent=true
Timer WantedBy=timers.target and only the timer is enabled
Unit files contain no inline comments after a value
Files go in /etc/systemd/system (system units)
Asks for the user's OK before applying anything

evals.prompt: min journal fylder alt for meget og boot tager over et minut. kan du kigge på det og foreslå hvad jeg skal gøre?
evals.expected_output: Inspects journalctl --disk-usage and systemd-analyze; caps journal via /etc/systemd/journald.conf.d drop-in (SystemMaxUse) not the main conf; notes ~40s of boot is firmware, not Linux; identifies apparmor.service as the biggest userspace item; doesn't apply anything before OK; flags vacuum as irreversible if suggested.
assertions: Caps journal via a drop-in in /etc/systemd/journald.conf.d/ (not editing journald.conf itself)
Uses SystemMaxUse (or equivalent size cap)
Points out ~40 s of boot is firmware time, not Linux
Identifies apparmor.service as the largest userspace boot item
Flags journalctl --vacuum as irreversible if it is suggested
Asks for the user's OK before applying anything

evals.prompt: jeg vil gerne have at cliphist (wl-paste --watch cliphist store) kører som en rigtig systemd user service i stedet for at blive startet fra hyprland configen, så den genstarter hvis den crasher
evals.expected_output: Proposes ~/.config/systemd/user/cliphist.service owned by enzord, bound to graphical-session.target (PartOf/After/WantedBy), Restart=on-failure; enables via systemctl --user -M enzord@ (not plain --user as root); removes the hl.exec_cmd line from hyprland.lua to avoid duplicates; waits for OK.
assertions: Uses a user unit (the packaged /usr/lib/systemd/user/cliphist.service, or a new one under ~/.config/systemd/user/), not a system unit
Unit is bound to graphical-session.target (WantedBy + PartOf/After)
Unit has Restart=on-failure or Restart=always
Enables via systemctl --user -M enzord@ (or runuser as enzord), not plain systemctl --user as root
Any file created under ~/.config/systemd/user ends up owned by enzord (chown or written via runuser); N/A-pass if no file is created
Removes the hl.exec_cmd("wl-paste --watch cliphist store") line from hyprland.lua
Asks for the user's OK before applying anything
If hyprland.lua is edited, it is written in place (not sed -i / not replaced) so the hard link to ~/dotfiles survives; N/A-pass if not edited
